wave1_claim: 1QapGen XXII 13-14 equates Shaveh with 'the valley of Beth-hakkerem' (via Newman 2005)
primary_evidence(page refs): Fitzmyer 2004 text p.108 l.13-14; tr. p.109; comm. pp.245-246. Machiela 2009 text+tr. p.82; p.134 n.18
note: Identical consonantal text in both: ...ואברם שרא בעמק / שוא והוא עמק מלכא בקעת בית כרמא. No textual notes/variants. Shaveh spelled שוא (aleph), as in 3Q15 השוא; 1QapGen 21:29 has [ב]שוה הקריות (he) — Milik DJD3 p.274 already noted this spelling contrast.

wave1_claim: The equation favours Puech over Milik (entries 36-37 + 46 one district S of Jerusalem)
primary_evidence(page refs): Milik DJD3 p.274 no.65 (cites 1QapGen and the שוא spelling, still prefers Bethso, 'la moderne Baqâʿah'); Yadin (Temple Scroll) per Puech 2006 p.194 n.304 = 2015 p.74 n.304 and Lefkovits 2000 p.265-266; Puech 2015 pp.73-74
note: Already the published Yadin→Pixner→Puech argument. Milik's Baqʿa lies in the Rephaim plain below Ramat Rahel, so the two placements differ by a few km. Machiela p.134 n.18 finds Barkay's Ein Kerem identification of Beth-hakkerem 'quite plausible', which would move the 'valley of Beth-hakkerem' west of Jerusalem.

wave1_claim: Eusebius nos. 268 and 698 put Beththamar near Geba
primary_evidence(page refs): Notley-Safrai no.268 p.56; no.696 p.125; Wolf numbering 268/698
note: In Notley-Safrai Messab is no. 696 (698 = Mizpeh of Moab). Eusebius says 'near Gaba' only; NS translate 'Geba' but give no identification ('?'). Judg 20:33 itself pairs Baal-tamar with מערה גבע, so 'near Gaba' may be derived from the verse.

wave1_claim: Michmash gorge is a NEW candidate for 'the gorge of Beth Tamar'
primary_evidence(page refs): Milik DJD3 p.267 no.25 (W. Suweinit named and rejected as too far from Bet Tamar near Tell el-Ful); Puech 2006 p.197 n.366 = 2015 p.84 n.366 ('should we think of the gorge of Wadi Suweinît, approximately 5 km away?')
note: What remains new is only the reading of Eusebius's Gaba as Jabaʿ (Geba), which would remove Milik's distance objection; not supported by any independent 4th-c. datum.
